annotation.title_clean: Possible consensus recommendations in relation to the clarification, consideration and development of aspects on the normative and operational framework on emerging technologies in the area of lethal autonomous weapons systems
annotation.title_en: Possible consensus recommendations in relation to the clarification, consideration and development of aspects on the normative and operational framework on emerging technologies in the area of lethal autonomous weapons systems
annotation.authors_or_issuer: France (working paper submitted to the CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS)
annotation.venue: UN CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS (CCW/GGE.1/2021/WP.4)
annotation.summary_en: French working paper to the CCW Group of Governmental Experts proposing consensus recommendations for a normative framework on lethal autonomous weapons. It distinguishes fully autonomous systems, which states should commit not to develop or use, from partially autonomous ones, to be regulated nationally through legal review, testing, training, accountability and human control.
key_provisions_or_claims: Framework should cover only lethal autonomous weapons systems, excluding remotely piloted and low-level autonomy systems.
Distinguishes fully from partially autonomous lethal weapons as objects needing different measures.
States should commit not to develop, acquire or use fully autonomous lethal weapons.
Partially autonomous systems regulated nationally via legal review, verification and validation, training, and chain of responsibility.
Humans must define rules of engagement and make critical decisions over use of force; framework should not unduly hamper dual-use technology.
